source_study.citation: Ambuehl, S.; Bernheim, B.D.; Ockenfels, A. (2021), What Motivates Paternalism? An Experimental Study, American Economic Review 111(3):787-830
source_study.sample_description_from_repository: Laboratory experiment, student subjects, University of Cologne
source_study.finding_from_original_article_abstract: Choice architects often remove impatient options to steer choosers toward the architect's ideals despite possibility of advice. This does not measure original-B persistent identity, or strong-A profitable exploitation.

source_host_migration.official_guidance: Data access may require ICPSR sign-in and agreement to terms; no user credentials obtained.

negative_results_and_transfer.source_claim_supported: In this specific Cologne lab paradigm, the authors report ideals-projective choice-menu intervention even where advice exists.
RVD_interpretation_not_supported: original B numerical identity or enduring subjective experience
long-term voluntary coexistence of actual artificial agents
preservation when power is overwhelming and exploitation is financially dominant
rejection of all image/warm-glow/future-instrumental motive alternatives
negative_results_and_transfer.core_discrimination: A's belief that restricting choice benefits B vs actual B choice rights; descriptive paternalism is not causal estimate of intrinsic value of original B's autonomy.
